extraction.name: ARC (AI2 Reasoning Challenge)
extraction.description: The AI2 Reasoning Challenge (ARC) is a question set, text corpus, and baselines for advanced question answering research. The ARC dataset consists of 7,787 natural science questions (non-diagram, multiple choice, typically 4-way) drawn from standardized tests authored for human use. It is partitioned into a Challenge Set (2,590 questions, answered incorrectly by both a retrieval-based algorithm and a word co-occurrence algorithm) and an Easy Set (5,197 questions). The release also includes the ARC Corpus, a corpus of 14M science sentences relevant to the task, and three baseline neural models (DecompAttn, BiDAF, and DGEM).
extraction.creator: Peter Clark, Isaac Cowhey, Oren Etzioni, Tushar Khot, Ashish Sabharwal, Carissa Schoenick, Oyvind Tafjord
extraction.citeAs: Clark, P., Cowhey, I., Etzioni, O., Khot, T., Sabharwal, A., Schoenick, C., & Tafjord, O. (2018). Think you have Solved Question Answering? Try ARC, the AI2 Reasoning Challenge. arXiv:1803.05457.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The ARC dataset was assembled by several months of extensive search and investigation to obtain natural grade-school science questions authored for standardized tests. Questions were drawn from a variety of sources including state educational testing programs (e.g., ACTAAP, AIMS, MCAS, NY Regents, TIMSS) and an anonymous content partner of AI2. The dataset was then partitioned into a Challenge Set and an Easy Set based on performance of a retrieval-based (IR) solver and a Pointwise Mutual Information (PMI) solver. The ARC Corpus was created by running large series of search queries relevant to science, automatically constructed by instantiating ~100 hand-written templates for ~80 science topics covered by US elementary and middle schools. The top documents from each search were collected, de-duplicated, stripped to text, and chunked into sentences. The corpus was augmented with the AristoMini corpus.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Document analysis, Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Natural grade-school science questions from standardized tests, drawn from sources such as ACTAAP, AIMS, Alaska Department of Education, AMP, CA Standards Test, FCAT, LA Ed Assm. Prog, MD School Assm., MCAS, MEA, MEAP, Mercury (anonymous AI2 content partner), MSA, NAEP, NC READY, NY Regents, Ohio Achievement Tests, TAKS, TIMSS, VA Stds of Learning, WASL. The ARC Corpus was mined from the Web via search engine queries relevant to science, augmented with the AristoMini corpus (Wiktionary definitions, Simple Wikipedia science articles, additional Web-collected science sentences).
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For the ARC Corpus: top documents from each search were collected and de-duplicated, content was stripped down to text, and text was chunked into sentences. Approximately 75% of a sampled 805 documents were judged as 'science relevant'. For defining the Challenge vs. Easy partition, questions were run through an IR solver (using the Waterloo corpus) and a PMI solver; questions answered incorrectly by both were put into the Challenge Set, the rest into the Easy Set.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Questions were pre-authored by standardized-test examiners for human tests, with correct answers already known. Grade-level labels were assigned by the examiners who authored the questions. For the analysis of knowledge and reasoning types, a sample of 100 questions was manually categorized by the authors into broad classes.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Categorization of knowledge and reasoning types is approximate, as it requires subjective judgement about the main challenge exhibited by different questions.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Elasticsearch (for IR-based filtering); proprietary chunker and Open IE (for DGEM baseline structure extraction).
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The ARC Dataset, Corpus, baseline models, and leaderboard are available at http://data.allenai.org/arc. A leaderboard is maintained for submitting new entries.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Baseline solvers beyond IR have a retrieval bias toward sentences very similar to the question, and away from sentences that individually only partially match the question but together fully explain the answer. The dataset's Challenge Set partition is defined by the failure of specific IR and PMI algorithms, which may introduce a bias toward questions those specific methods cannot solve.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Questions are restricted to non-diagram, multiple-choice natural science questions at grade-school level (grades 3-9). The Challenge Set partition is defined operationally via two specific baseline solvers (IR and PMI), which only approximates the notion of 'hard' questions. Although the ARC Corpus mentions knowledge relevant to ~95% of Challenge questions, exploiting this knowledge with simple retrieval methods is non-trivial. 11 question words (mainly proper nouns) do not appear in the corpus.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Development, and Testing for question answering research. Intended to encourage AI research in advanced question answering requiring reasoning, commonsense knowledge, and deeper text comprehension beyond surface-level retrieval. The dataset is split into Train (3,370), Dev (869), and Test (3,548) partitions. Use of the ARC Corpus is optional, and systems are not restricted to this corpus.
